title: A Black Box Optimization-based Bidding Strategy for Data Consumers in Auction-based Federated Learning

problem.claim: Determining optimal bidding strategies for Data Consumers in Auction-based Federated Learning is a fundamental challenge.

gap.claim: Reinforcement-learning approaches face credit-assignment ambiguity and non-stationarity because stepwise Markovian rewards do not match delayed, trajectory-level utility in federated-learning training.

contributions.claim: The paper reformulates Auction-based Federated Learning bidding as a Black-Box Optimization problem, treating the recruitment-to-training pipeline as a single function evaluation.

BBO-AFL introduces Budget-Aware Exploration, which separates high-frequency market cost signals from low-frequency model-utility feedback and projects risky perturbations onto a financially safe manifold using a closed-form KKT solution.
The paper provides a theoretical analysis of asymptotic convergence-rate recovery for zeroth-order methods while maintaining financial safety along the optimization trajectory.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on benchmark datasets reportedly show that BBO-AFL significantly outperforms state-of-the-art reinforcement-learning baselines.
The authors report a 2.1% improvement in model accuracy.
The authors report a 60% reduction in training cycles needed to reach target accuracy, described as superior economic sample efficiency.

narrative_sequence.summary: Auction-based Federated Learning is presented as a paradigm for incentivizing private-resource contributions to a global model.
The paper identifies optimal Data Consumer bidding as a challenge and attributes limitations of existing reinforcement-learning approaches to reward-structure mismatch.
The authors reformulate bidding as black-box optimization and propose BBO-AFL with Budget-Aware Exploration for cost-aware policy sampling.
The paper reports convergence and financial-safety properties for the proposed optimization process.
Benchmark experiments are reported to outperform reinforcement-learning baselines in accuracy and training-cycle efficiency.
